titleStmt.title: Introduction to the human gut microbiota
titleStmt.author: Elizabeth Thursby
Nathalie Juge

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Introduction to the human gut microbiota

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the composition and development of the human gastrointestinal microbiota and its effect on gut integrity and host health
span.quote: The collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract is termed the ‘gut microbiota’ and has co-evolved with the host over thousands of years to form an intricate and mutually beneficial relationship

span.label: what is currently understood about how the human gut microbiota develops, what it is composed of, and what its alteration does
span.quote: This review summarises our current understanding of the development and composition of the human GI microbiota, and its impact on gut integrity and host health, underlying the need for mechanistic studies focusing on host–microbe interactions.

span.label: a review that states the CONDITIONS under which its own field's findings can be interpreted - inter-individual variation, heterogeneity along the tract, functional redundancy, and cause against effect in dysbiosis
span.quote: The interpretation of these studies relies on a better understanding of inter-individual variations, heterogeneity of bacterial communities along and across the GI tract, functional redundancy and the need to distinguish cause from effect in states of dysbiosis.

span.label: critique
span.quote: The interpretation of these studies relies on a better understanding of inter-individual variations, heterogeneity of bacterial communities along and across the GI tract, functional redundancy and the need to distinguish cause from effect in states of dysbiosis.

span.label: a microbial community that co-evolved with the host, whose altered composition is associated with inflammatory disease
span.quote: However, there is potential for these mechanisms to be disrupted as a result of an altered microbial composition, known as dysbiosis.

span.label: narrative review of composition and development studies, contrasting culture-based knowledge with sequencing-based surveys
span.term: narrative review of composition and development studies, contrasting culture-based knowledge with sequencing-based surveys
span.quote: Around a decade ago, most knowledge about the adult human gut microbiota stemmed from labour-intensive culture-based methods

span.label: the microbiota strengthens gut integrity, shapes the intestinal epithelium, harvests energy, protects against pathogens and regulates host immunity - and disruption of those mechanisms by an altered composition is what `dysbiosis` names
span.quote: The microbiota offers many benefits to the host, through a range of physiological functions such as strengthening gut integrity or shaping the intestinal epithelium \ [7\], harvesting energy \ [8\], protecting against pathogens \ [9\] and regulating host immunity

span.label: fibre deficiency makes the community switch to eating the host's own secreted mucins, which thins the mucus barrier and lets pathogens reach the epithelium
span.quote: The erosion of the colonic mucus barrier under dietary fibre deficiency is associated with a switch of the gut microbiota towards the utilisation of secreted mucins as a nutrient source \ [83\].

span.label: cross-feeding: acetate or lactate produced by one species is converted to butyrate by another, so fermentation products do not accumulate
span.quote: For example, acetate produced by fermentation of resistant starch by _R. bromii_ \ [103\] or lactate produced by lactic acid bacteria such as lactobacilli and bifidobacteria provides substrate for other microbiota members such as _Eubacterium hallii_ and _Anaerostipes caccae_ which convert it into butyrate \ [104, 105\].

span.label: a decreasing butyrate gradient from lumen to crypt is proposed to control epithelial turnover - proliferation at the crypt bottom, apoptosis nearer the lumen
span.quote: A decreasing gradient of butyrate from lumen to crypt is suggested to control intestinal epithelial turnover and homeostasis by promoting colonocyte proliferation at the bottom of crypts, whilst increasing apoptosis and exfoliation of cells closer to the lumen \ [144\].

span.label: antibiotics liberate fucose and sialic acid from mucins, and the pathogens that cannot cleave those sugars themselves expand on what the commensals released
span.quote: For example, _S._ Typhimurium and _C. difficile_ utilise fucose and sialic acid liberated by the gut microbiota, and increasing sialic acid levels post-antibiotic treatment favour their expansion within the gut \ [135\].

span.label: bacteria without a sialidase carry a nan cluster instead and depend on other members of the community for their carbon - dependence as a structural feature, not a deficiency
span.quote: Many bacteria, including pathogens such as _Salmonella_ Typhimurium or _C. difficile_, lack a sialidase but harbour a ‘nan cluster’ dedicated to sialic acid metabolism, and thus rely on other members of the gut microbiota to provide them with this source of carbon \ [107\].

span.label: the germ-free deficit in CD4+ T-cell expansion is reversed completely by a single molecule, polysaccharide A from the B. fragilis capsule
span.quote: This deficiency can be completely reversed by the treatment of GF mice with polysaccharide A from the capsule of _B. fragilis_ \ [163\].

span.label: host FUT2 genotype decides whether H and ABO antigens appear in the mucosa, and that host genetic difference shifts the abundance of many bacterial groups
span.quote: For example, the presence (secretor) or absence (non-secretor) of H and ABO antigens in GI mucosa, determined by the FUT2 genotype (a gene expressing an α1,2-fucosyltransferase), affects the abundance of many bacterial groups \ [78\].

span.label: THE ABSTRACT NAMES FOUR CONDITIONS ON READING ITS OWN LITERATURE: inter-individual variation, heterogeneity of communities along and across the tract, functional redundancy, and THE NEED TO DISTINGUISH CAUSE FROM EFFECT IN DYSBIOSIS
span.quote: The interpretation of these studies relies on a better understanding of inter-individual variations, heterogeneity of bacterial communities along and across the GI tract, functional redundancy and the need to distinguish cause from effect in states of dysbiosis.

span.label: the existence and formation of enterotypes is called CONTROVERSIAL in the sentence immediately after they are described - a hedge the later literature drops
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: the field needs mechanistic studies of host-microbe interaction, which the review states as the reason it was written
span.quote: This review summarises our current understanding of the development and composition of the human GI microbiota, and its impact on gut integrity and host health, underlying the need for mechanistic studies focusing on host–microbe interactions.

span.label: inter-individual differences in species arrangement are proposed to OUTWEIGH the within-individual differences, so a between-person comparison carries most of the variance in any composition study
span.quote: Inter-individual differences in the species and subspecies arrangement are proposed to outweigh differences in the community arrangement within an individual

span.label: A. muciniphila is credited with protection against several inflammatory diseases and the paper states the mechanism is not established
span.quote: suggesting that this strain possesses anti-inflammatory properties although the underlying mechanisms have not been completely elucidated \ [171\].

span.label: whether dysbiosis causes disease or follows from it is left open, and the paper says the answer changes which strategy is needed
span.quote: Whether dysbiosis of the microbiota is a cause or a consequence of the disease is therefore likely to exacerbate the progression of the disease and affect the type of strategies needed to restore symbiosis.

span.label: the effects of antibiotics and the recovery time are individual-dependent, which the paper attributes to pre-treatment variation between people
span.quote: The exact effects and the time for recovery of the microbiota following antibiotic administration appear to be individual-dependent, a likely effect of the inter-individual variation in the microbiota prior to treatment \ [33, 47, 132\].

span.label: complex carbohydrate breakdown by gut species is stated to be more complex than the field previously suggested
span.quote: revealed that the recognition and breakdown of complex carbohydrates, such as xylan, mannan, xyloglucan or starch, by the human gut microbiota is significantly more complex than previously suggested \ [91– 96\].

span.label: the widely repeated 10:1 cell ratio is given together with the revised estimate that contradicts it, rather than either alone
span.note: eliminates: a superseded figure being carried forward as current because it is the one everybody cites · outcome: held
span.quote: The number of microorganisms inhabiting the GI tract has been estimated to exceed 1014, which encompasses ∼10 times more bacterial cells than the number of human cells and over 100 times the amount of genomic content (microbiome) as the human genome \ [2, 4\]. However, a recently revised estimate has suggested that the ratio of human:bacterial cells is actually closer to 1:1

span.label: within-individual variation is compared with between-individual variation before composition differences are attributed to anything
span.note: eliminates: inter-individual variance being read as an effect of an exposure · outcome: held
span.quote: Inter-individual differences in the species and subspecies arrangement are proposed to outweigh differences in the community arrangement within an individual

span.label: gut microbiota
span.quote: The collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract is termed the ‘gut microbiota’ and has co-evolved with the host over thousands of years to form an intricate and mutually beneficial relationship

span.label: enterotype
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: core microbiota
span.quote: Suggestions have been made of the presence of a ‘core microbiota’, proposed to be a set of the same abundant organisms present in all individuals. However, more similarity can be observed in the repertoire of microbial genes present between individuals than the taxonomic profile, suggesting that the core microbiota may be better defined at a functional rather than organism level

span.label: dysbiosis
span.quote: However, there is potential for these mechanisms to be disrupted as a result of an altered microbial composition, known as dysbiosis.

span.label: superorganism
span.quote: As a result of the vast number of bacterial cells in the body, the host and the microorganisms inhabiting it are often referred to as a ‘superorganism’

span.label: community types
span.quote: Recently, it has been possible to classify individual microbiota arrangements into ‘community types’ that can be predictive of each other and are associated with background

span.label: microbiota-accessible carbohydrates
span.quote: Shaping of the colonic microbiota is subject to the availability of microbiota-accessible carbohydrates (MACs) that are found in dietary fibre.

span.label: cross-feeding
span.quote: Microbial cross-feeding is one mechanism proposed to mediate this effect.

span.label: glycoside hydrolases
span.quote: The capacity of gut bacteria to utilise dietary or mucin glycans is dictated by the repertoire of glycoside hydrolases (GHs) and polysaccharide lyases (PLs) encoded by their genomes \ [70\].

span.label: segmented filamentous bacteria
span.quote: Dysbiosis of the microbiota, in particular an over-representation of segmented filamentous bacteria (SFB), occurs in mice deficient in IgA, an effect that may be particularly damaging to the host due to the ability of SFB to strongly adhere to the epithelium and activate the immune system \ [127\].

span.label: functional redundancy
span.quote: whilst species-specific effects are less probable due to the high amount of functional redundancy within the microbiota \ [52, 116– 119\].

span.label: pattern recognition receptors
span.quote: This process is mainly performed via the pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) of epithelial cells, such as Toll-like or Nod-like receptors, which are able to recognise the molecular effectors that are produced by intestinal microbes.

span.label: secretory IgA
span.quote: Secretory IgA (SIgA), another component of the immune system, co-localises with gut bacteria in the outer mucus layer and assists in limiting the exposure of the epithelial cell surface to bacteria \ [120, 124\].

span.label: gnotobiotic
span.quote: Recent studies using gnotobiotic mice showed that certain microbial species can be used to restore growth impairments transmitted by microbiota from malnourished children, raising the possibility of using these species as a therapeutic intervention to counteract the negative effects of undernutrition \ [67– 69\].

span.label: gut microbiota - AS DEFINED HERE: the collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract, co-evolved with the host - the term covers three domains and not only bacteria
span.quote: The collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract is termed the ‘gut microbiota’ and has co-evolved with the host over thousands of years to form an intricate and mutually beneficial relationship

span.label: core microbiota - proposed as a set of the same abundant ORGANISMS present in all individuals, and relocated in the same sentence: better defined at a FUNCTIONAL than an organism level, because gene repertoires agree where taxonomies do not
span.quote: Suggestions have been made of the presence of a ‘core microbiota’, proposed to be a set of the same abundant organisms present in all individuals. However, more similarity can be observed in the repertoire of microbial genes present between individuals than the taxonomic profile, suggesting that the core microbiota may be better defined at a functional rather than organism level

span.label: dysbiosis - an altered microbial composition that disrupts the microbiota's physiological functions; the direction of causation is named as an open question in this paper's own abstract
span.quote: However, there is potential for these mechanisms to be disrupted as a result of an altered microbial composition, known as dysbiosis.

span.label: critiques → the enterotype classification, on the ground that the evidence for the existence and formation of enterotypes is controversial - a hedge rinninella2019 does not carry, in a paper it cites
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: critiques → the dysbiosis-and-disease literature, on the ground that it has not distinguished cause from effect
span.quote: The interpretation of these studies relies on a better understanding of inter-individual variations, heterogeneity of bacterial communities along and across the GI tract, functional redundancy and the need to distinguish cause from effect in states of dysbiosis.

span.label: corrects → the 10:1 bacteria-to-human-cell ratio, which a revised estimate puts closer to 1:1 - printed in the sentence after the original figure
span.quote: The number of microorganisms inhabiting the GI tract has been estimated to exceed 1014, which encompasses ∼10 times more bacterial cells than the number of human cells and over 100 times the amount of genomic content (microbiome) as the human genome \ [2, 4\]. However, a recently revised estimate has suggested that the ratio of human:bacterial cells is actually closer to 1:1

span.label: THE EXISTENCE AND FORMATION OF ENTEROTYPES IS CONTROVERSIAL - stated immediately after the three enterotypes are described from 33 samples
span.term: THE EXISTENCE AND FORMATION OF ENTEROTYPES IS CONTROVERSIAL - stated immediately after the three enterotypes are described from 33 samples
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: the 10:1 bacteria-to-human-cell ratio has been revised to approximately 1:1, and this paper prints the revision in the sentence after the original figure
span.term: the 10:1 bacteria-to-human-cell ratio has been revised to approximately 1:1, and this paper prints the revision in the sentence after the original figure
span.quote: The number of microorganisms inhabiting the GI tract has been estimated to exceed 1014, which encompasses ∼10 times more bacterial cells than the number of human cells and over 100 times the amount of genomic content (microbiome) as the human genome \ [2, 4\]. However, a recently revised estimate has suggested that the ratio of human:bacterial cells is actually closer to 1:1

span.label: the core microbiota may be better defined at a FUNCTIONAL than an organism level, because gene repertoires are more similar between individuals than taxonomies are
span.term: the core microbiota may be better defined at a FUNCTIONAL than an organism level, because gene repertoires are more similar between individuals than taxonomies are
span.quote: Suggestions have been made of the presence of a ‘core microbiota’, proposed to be a set of the same abundant organisms present in all individuals. However, more similarity can be observed in the repertoire of microbial genes present between individuals than the taxonomic profile, suggesting that the core microbiota may be better defined at a functional rather than organism level

span.label: interpreting the dysbiosis literature requires distinguishing cause from effect, which the paper names as a condition rather than a caveat
span.term: interpreting the dysbiosis literature requires distinguishing cause from effect, which the paper names as a condition rather than a caveat
span.quote: The interpretation of these studies relies on a better understanding of inter-individual variations, heterogeneity of bacterial communities along and across the GI tract, functional redundancy and the need to distinguish cause from effect in states of dysbiosis.

span.label: Bacteroidetes carry roughly three and a half times as many glycan-cleaving enzymes per genome as Firmicutes
span.quote: Bacteroidetes encode many more glycan-cleaving enzymes (137.1 GH and PL genes per genome) than Firmicutes members (39.6 GH and PL genes per genome) \ [89\].

span.label: one gut bacterium encodes more than twice as many glycoside hydrolases as the entire human genome
span.quote: The _Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron_ genome contains 260 GHs, in comparison with the 97 hydrolases encoded by humans \ [90\].

span.label: diet tracks the phylum-level composition: African children on starch and fibre carry far more Actinobacteria and Bacteroidetes than European children on sugar and animal protein
span.quote: Infants from rural Africa, with a diet dominated by starch, fibre and plant polysaccharides, harbour a microbiota that is abundant in the Actinobacteria (10.1%) and Bacteroidetes (57.7%) phyla \ [63\].

span.label: a mucin-degrading species prevents diet-induced obesity in mice and reduces metabolic inflammation, and the effect survives pasteurising the bacterium
span.quote: The protective role of _A. muciniphila_ could be recapitulated using _A. muciniphila_ purified membrane protein or the pasteurised bacterium \ [86\].

span.label: restoring diversity after a low-fibre diet needs the missing taxa as well as the carbohydrates - feeding alone does not bring them back
span.quote: Restoration of diversity requires administration of MACs in combination with the bacterial taxa that were missing \ [66\].

span.label: germ-free mice have an extremely thin colonic mucus layer and bacterial products alone restore its thickness
span.quote: Mice housed under germ-free conditions have an extremely thin adherent colonic mucus layer, but when exposed to bacterial products (peptidoglycan or LPS), the thickness of the adherent mucus layer can be restored to levels observed in conventionally reared mice \ [158\]. _B. thetaiotaomicron_ and _F. prausnitzii_ have been implicated in the co-ordination of mucus production \ [159\]. _R. gnavus_ E1, _Lactobacillus casei_ DN-114 001 and _B. thetaiotaomicron_ are able to remodel mucin glycosylation, for example, by modulating glycosyltransferase expression \ [160– 162\].

span.label: the collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract, co-evolved with the host into a mutually beneficial relationship
span.quote: The collection of bacteria, archaea and eukarya colonising the GI tract is termed the ‘gut microbiota’ and has co-evolved with the host over thousands of years to form an intricate and mutually beneficial relationship

span.label: an altered microbial composition that disrupts the microbiota's physiological functions
span.quote: However, there is potential for these mechanisms to be disrupted as a result of an altered microbial composition, known as dysbiosis.

span.label: a set of the same abundant organisms present in all individuals - which the same passage says may be better defined at a functional rather than organism level
span.quote: Suggestions have been made of the presence of a ‘core microbiota’, proposed to be a set of the same abundant organisms present in all individuals. However, more similarity can be observed in the repertoire of microbial genes present between individuals than the taxonomic profile, suggesting that the core microbiota may be better defined at a functional rather than organism level

span.label: microbiota-accessible carbohydrates, defined by where they are found
span.quote: Shaping of the colonic microbiota is subject to the availability of microbiota-accessible carbohydrates (MACs) that are found in dietary fibre.

span.label: the intestinal barrier stated as three integrated components - physical, biochemical and immunological
span.quote: The barrier comprises several integrated components including physical (the epithelial and mucus layers), biochemical (enzymes and antimicrobial proteins) and immunological (IgA and epithelia-associated immune cells) factors \ [51\].

span.label: the two colonic mucus layers, one sterile and impermeable, one penetrable and colonised
span.quote: Colonic mucus is divided into two layers consisting of a dense and impermeable inner layer and a loose outer coating which is penetrable by bacteria \ [74\].

span.label: the revised human:bacterial cell ratio, against the ~10:1 the same paragraph quotes from the earlier literature
span.quote: The number of microorganisms inhabiting the GI tract has been estimated to exceed 1014, which encompasses ∼10 times more bacterial cells than the number of human cells and over 100 times the amount of genomic content (microbiome) as the human genome \ [2, 4\]. However, a recently revised estimate has suggested that the ratio of human:bacterial cells is actually closer to 1:1

span.label: square metres - the GI tract as one of the largest interfaces in the human body, with around 60 tonnes of food passing through it in a lifetime
span.quote: The human gastrointestinal (GI) tract represents one of the largest interfaces (250–400 m2) between the host, environmental factors and antigens in the human body. In an average life time, around 60 tonnes of food pass through the human GI tract, along with an abundance of microorganisms from the environment which impose a huge threat on gut integrity

span.label: samples from different nationalities - the multi-dimensional analysis the three enterotypes were derived from
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: glycan-cleaving genes per genome, Bacteroidetes against Firmicutes
span.quote: Bacteroidetes encode many more glycan-cleaving enzymes (137.1 GH and PL genes per genome) than Firmicutes members (39.6 GH and PL genes per genome) \ [89\].

span.label: the proportion of the three predominant short-chain fatty acids in the GI tract
span.quote: Three predominant SCFAs, propionate, butyrate and acetate, are typically found in a proportion of 1:1:3 in the GI tract \ [137\].

span.label: the share of Muc2 molecular mass accounted for by O-glycans
span.quote: Collectively, _O_-glycans account for up to 80% of the total molecular mass of Muc2/MUC2 \ [73\].

span.label: ratio
span.quote: The number of microorganisms inhabiting the GI tract has been estimated to exceed 1014, which encompasses ∼10 times more bacterial cells than the number of human cells and over 100 times the amount of genomic content (microbiome) as the human genome \ [2, 4\]. However, a recently revised estimate has suggested that the ratio of human:bacterial cells is actually closer to 1:1

span.label: microbial composition
span.quote: However, there is potential for these mechanisms to be disrupted as a result of an altered microbial composition, known as dysbiosis.

span.label: nationality
span.quote: Multi-dimensional analysis of 33 samples from different nationalities revealed the presence of three enterotypes identifiable by variations in the level of one of three genera: _Bacteroides_ (enterotype 1), _Prevotella_ (enterotype 2) and _Ruminococcus_ (enterotype 3) \ [49\]. However, evidence surrounding the existence and formation of these enterotypes is controversial

span.label: the FUT2 secretor genotype as a host variable that shifts bacterial abundance
span.quote: For example, the presence (secretor) or absence (non-secretor) of H and ABO antigens in GI mucosa, determined by the FUT2 genotype (a gene expressing an α1,2-fucosyltransferase), affects the abundance of many bacterial groups \ [78\].

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1042/bcj20160510.
